items.name: Kerala Ash Gourd Mung Olan
steps: Measure 850 ml (about 3 1/2 cups) water for Kerala Ash Gourd Mung Olan; bring it to a full boil, then keep it covered and hot for the additions below.
Cover the mung beans with at least three times its volume of cool water and soak for 30 minutes; drain for 2 minutes before the first heated step.
Simmer the soaked mung until it begins to soften. Maintain moderate heat for 16–18 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until the pulses crush easily against the side of the pot.
Slide in the ash-gourd batons without breaking them. Take 8–10 minutes over medium-low heat, using the stated texture and aroma as the final guide.

Grind the grated coconut with a ladle of hot cooking liquid and fold the pale cream into the tender vegetables. Work in 3 short pulses, pausing between them so the mixture stays cool and retains the intended texture.

Draw the pot from the heat, season gently, and perfume the surface with torn curry leaves and coconut oil. Leave the pan off the flame for 4 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Rest Kerala Ash Gourd Mung Olan for 5 minutes covered off the burner; stir once gently, check the final consistency, and serve warm without prolonged holding.
items.guidance: This mild, moist Kerala-style olan is especially gentle when served freshly cooked Vata: serve it warm and add a little ghee if the meal feels dry. Pitta: keep the sharp spices modest and favor coriander or fennel. Kapha: use a smaller portion and sharpen the seasoning with ginger or black pepper.

items.name: Kerala Pumpkin and Pea Olan
steps: Measure 620 ml (about 2 1/2 cups) water for Kerala Pumpkin and Pea Olan; bring it to a full boil, then keep it covered and hot for the additions below.
Cook the pumpkin cubes with the crushed cumin until their edges are soft but their centers still hold shape. Aim for an even 2–3 mm thickness; repair cracks before the piece reaches the hot surface.
Add the peas and a smooth coconut paste. Keep the pan over gentle medium heat for 2–3 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.
Simmer quietly so the vegetables take up the creamy broth. Maintain low heat for 11–13 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a spoon drawn across the base leaves a trail that closes slowly.
Turn off the flame before drizzling over the coconut oil and scattering the torn curry leaves. Keep the layer loose and even, with no pooled liquid, so every portion receives the same balance.
Rest Kerala Pumpkin and Pea Olan for 5 minutes covered off the burner; stir once gently, check the final consistency, and serve warm without prolonged holding.

items.name: Kerala Cabbage Carrot Thoran
steps: Lay out the prepared cabbage, carrot, and fresh coconut in their order of use; drain wet components for 2 minutes before they reach hot fat.
Crackle the mustard in coconut oil. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over low heat for 4–5 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.
Wake the curry leaves and turmeric in the fragrant pan. Take 8–10 minutes over steady low heat, using the stated texture and aroma as the final guide.

Toss in the shredded cabbage and carrot matchsticks, cover briefly. Keep the pot covered over moderate heat for 7–9 minutes; check once at the midpoint and continue until the leaves wilt but still retain their color.
Let their own steam soften them. Allow 5–7 minutes at medium-low heat, checking whether a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.

Uncover while the vegetables remain bright, fold through the grated coconut. Keep the pan over gentle medium heat for 1–2 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.
Season before serving. Leave the pan off the flame for 6 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Rest Kerala Cabbage Carrot Thoran for 3 minutes uncovered off the burner; turn the pieces once, check that no steam is softening the surface, and serve warm.

items.name: Kerala Beet Coconut Thoran
steps: Measure 70 ml (about 1/4 cup) water for Kerala Beet Coconut Thoran; bring it to a full boil, then keep it covered and hot for the additions below.

Bloom the mustard and cumin in coconut oil. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over steady low heat for 3–4 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Add the slit chili and curry leaves for a brief sizzle. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over moderate heat for 4–5 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.

Stir the tiny beet pieces through the tempering, splash in a little hot water. Warm the fat over medium-low heat for 1 minute, let the spice sizzle for 30–45 seconds, and pour the tempering over the dish before its final rest.

Cover until just tender. Keep the pot covered over gentle medium heat for 19–21 minutes; check once at the midpoint and continue until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.

Let any remaining moisture evaporate before turning the grated coconut and salt through the ruby vegetables. Allow 8–10 minutes at low heat, checking whether a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.
Rest Kerala Beet Coconut Thoran for 3 minutes uncovered off the burner; turn the pieces once, check that no steam is softening the surface, and serve warm.

ingredients.name: Green beans, sliced into small rounds

Toast the split black gram in warm coconut oil until golden. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.
Let the mustard pop around it. Keep this stage to 7–9 minutes over gentle medium heat and stop when a knife tip enters the thickest stem with only slight resistance.
Add the bean rounds with turmeric and a small splash of hot water. Keep the pan over low heat for 2–3 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.

Cover only until the green color deepens. Keep the pot covered over gentle medium heat for 4–6 minutes; check once at the midpoint and continue until a knife tip enters the thickest stem with only slight resistance.

Finish uncovered with the coconut and torn curry leaves, stirring until the thoran is moist rather than wet. Leave the pan off the flame for 4 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.

items.name: Kerala Eggplant Theeyal
steps: Bring 520 ml (about 2 1/4 cups) water to a boil in a separate kettle and hold it hot, covered, so Kerala Eggplant Theeyal never loses its simmer.

Brown the coconut slowly with coriander and fenugreek until nutty. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over low heat for 2–3 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.
Grind the cooled mixture with a little hot water. Work in 3 short pulses, pausing between them so the mixture stays cool and retains the intended texture.

Sear the eggplant wedges in part of the oil, pour in the diluted tamarind. Use medium-high heat for 4–6 minutes, turning once, until the cut faces are browned while the centers remain firm enough for simmering.
Simmer until the flesh yields. Maintain medium-low heat for 10–12 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.

Stir in the roasted paste, reduce to a glossy gravy, and crown it with mustard and curry leaves crackled in the remaining oil. Maintain gentle medium heat for 8–10 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a spoon drawn across the base leaves a trail that closes slowly.
Rest Kerala Eggplant Theeyal for 5 minutes covered off the burner; stir once gently, check the final consistency, and serve warm without prolonged holding.

Rest Andhra Drumstick Peanut Kura for 3 minutes uncovered off the burner; turn the pieces once, check that no steam is softening the surface, and serve warm.

items.name: Karnataka Brown Rice Bisi Bele

ingredients.name: Green beans, cut into short pieces

steps: Prepare 1250 ml (about 5 1/4 cups) hot water before starting Karnataka Brown Rice Bisi Bele; keep one small ladle in reserve in case the base tightens early.
Cover the brown rice and pigeon pea with at least three times their combined volume of cool water and soak for 30 minutes; drain for 2 minutes before the first heated step.

Cook the soaked rice and pigeon pea together until both are soft enough to merge under a spoon. Maintain steady low heat for 17–19 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until the pulses crush easily against the side of the pot.

Simmer the carrot and beans with coriander, cinnamon, and diluted tamarind until the vegetables are tender. In a second pot while the grains cook, use medium-low heat for 10–12 minutes, stopping when a knife enters the largest vegetable piece without resistance.
Combine the two pots, loosen the mixture to a flowing consistency. Work over low heat for 4–6 minutes, folding from the bottom until the mixture is even, hot through, and no raw spice aroma remains.
Finish the bisi bele with salt and warm ghee. Leave the pan off the flame for 6 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Rest Karnataka Brown Rice Bisi Bele for 5 minutes covered off the burner; fluff the grains once, check the final consistency, and serve warm without prolonged holding.

items.name: Karnataka Dill Lentil Saaru
steps: Set aside 1050 ml (about 4 1/2 cups) freshly boiled water for Karnataka Dill Lentil Saaru, reserving about 60 ml to correct the final consistency.
Simmer the brown lentils with turmeric until tender. Maintain low heat for 15–17 minutes, stirring every 4 minutes, until the pulses crush easily against the side of the pot.
Whisk a small portion to give the broth body. Whisk for 50 seconds, scraping the bottom and corners until no dry pockets or lumps remain.

Add the chopped tomatoes and cracked pepper, cooking until their sharp raw scent disappears. Keep the pan over moderate heat for 2–3 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.

Bloom cumin in ghee, stir it into the saaru with the chopped dill, and stop cooking while the herb remains fragrant. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.
For Karnataka Dill Lentil Saaru, inspect the main component at minute 17; rotate the pot and add 30–60 ml hot water only if the base is tightening before it is tender.
Rest Karnataka Dill Lentil Saaru for 5 minutes covered off the burner; stir once gently, check the final consistency, and serve warm without prolonged holding.

items.name: Karnataka Chayote Majjige Huli

ingredients.name: Chayote, peeled and cut into chunks

steps: Measure 400 ml (about 1 3/4 cups) water for Karnataka Chayote Majjige Huli; bring it to a full boil, then keep it covered and hot for the additions below.
For Karnataka Chayote Majjige Huli, cover the chana dal with at least three times its volume of cool water and soak for 30 minutes; drain for 2 minutes before the first heated step.

Cook the chayote chunks with turmeric until tender enough to cut with the edge of a spoon. Maintain gentle medium heat for 11–13 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.

Grind the soaked chana dal with coconut and cumin, simmer this paste around the vegetable. Maintain low heat for 15–17 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until the pulses crush easily against the side of the pot.
Let it lose its raw taste. Allow 7–9 minutes at steady low heat, checking whether a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.
Lower the heat before folding in the whisked yogurt. Keep this stage to 8–10 minutes over moderate heat and stop when a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.

Finish without boiling with mustard and curry leaves tempered in coconut oil. Leave the pan off the flame for 6 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Rest Karnataka Chayote Majjige Huli for 5 minutes covered off the burner; stir once gently, check the final consistency, and serve warm without prolonged holding.

items.name: Karnataka Green Bean Coconut Palya

ingredients.name: Green beans, cut on a fine diagonal

steps: Heat 70 ml (about 1/4 cup) water until vigorously boiling, then lower it to a bare simmer beside the main pot for measured additions.

Brown the split black gram in coconut oil and wait for the mustard to pop before adding turmeric and curry leaves. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over medium-low heat for 4–5 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.
Toss in the diagonally cut beans with a splash of hot water. Work over low heat for 4–6 minutes, folding from the bottom until the mixture is even, hot through, and no raw spice aroma remains.

Cover until they are tender but still green. Keep the pot covered over low heat for 20–22 minutes; check once at the midpoint and continue until a knife tip enters the thickest stem with only slight resistance.

Cook off the remaining moisture, fold in the grated coconut. Maintain steady low heat for 9–11 minutes, stirring every 4 minutes, until a knife tip enters the thickest stem with only slight resistance.
Season the palya while it is hot. Leave the pan off the flame for 5 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Rest Karnataka Green Bean Coconut Palya for 3 minutes uncovered off the burner; turn the pieces once, check that no steam is softening the surface, and serve warm.

items.name: Karnataka Beet Sesame Palya
steps: Set aside 60 ml (about 1/4 cup) freshly boiled water for Karnataka Beet Sesame Palya, reserving about 60 ml to correct the final consistency.

Crackle mustard and cumin in coconut oil. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over moderate heat for 3–4 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.
Add the torn curry leaves without letting them scorch. Keep the pan over medium-low heat for 1–2 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.
Scatter in the coarse beet shreds, splash the pan with hot water. Keep the layer loose and even, with no pooled liquid, so every portion receives the same balance.

Cover until the raw crunch softens. Keep the pot covered over low heat for 19–21 minutes; check once at the midpoint and continue until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.
Uncover, toss with the ground sesame. Keep the pan over steady low heat for 2–3 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.
Cook until the palya is moist but no liquid pools beneath it. Maintain moderate heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.
Rest Karnataka Beet Sesame Palya for 3 minutes uncovered off the burner; turn the pieces once, check that no steam is softening the surface, and serve warm.

items.name: Karnataka Cabbage Pea Palya
steps: Lay out the prepared cabbage, green peas, and fresh coconut in their order of use; drain wet components for 2 minutes before they reach hot fat.
Pop the mustard in coconut oil. Keep the pan over medium heat for 30–45 seconds, covering it briefly if needed, until the seeds finish popping without darkening.
Add the slit chili and curry leaves for a short aromatic burst. Keep the pan over steady low heat for 2–3 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.

Tumble in the cabbage and peas, cover for a few minutes. Keep the pot covered over moderate heat for 6–8 minutes; check once at the midpoint and continue until the leaves wilt but still retain their color.
Let the vegetables soften in their own steam. Allow 4–6 minutes at medium-low heat, checking whether the aroma is rounded and the stated texture is reached.

Remove the lid while some bite remains, stir through the coconut and salt. Leave the pan off the flame for 5 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Serve the palya promptly. Leave the pan off the flame for 6 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.

items.name: Karnataka Methi Brown Rice Bath
steps: Prepare 700 ml (about 3 cups) hot water before starting Karnataka Methi Brown Rice Bath; keep one small ladle in reserve in case the base tightens early.
Cover the brown rice with at least three times its volume of cool water and soak for 30 minutes; drain for 2 minutes before the first heated step.
Soften the chopped fenugreek leaves in ghee with cumin until their raw bitterness mellows. Take 5–7 minutes over moderate heat, using the stated texture and aroma as the final guide.

Stir in the soaked rice, peas, coriander, and turmeric, coating every grain in the green mixture. Keep the pan over medium-low heat for 1–2 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.
Pour in hot water, cover. Bring the pot to a brisk simmer over medium-high heat for 3–5 minutes, then cover as bubbles reach the center and continue with the timed cook below.
Cook gently until the rice is tender. Maintain low heat for 17–19 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until a grain pressed between two fingers has no chalky center.
Rest the bath before fluffing and seasoning. Leave the pan off the flame for 6 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Rest Karnataka Methi Brown Rice Bath for 5 minutes covered off the burner; fluff the grains once, check the final consistency, and serve warm without prolonged holding.

items.name: Karnataka Lemon Jowar Chitranna
steps: Lay out the prepared sorghum grains, peanuts, and mustard seeds in their order of use; drain wet components for 2 minutes before they reach hot fat.

Separate the cooked sorghum grains on a platter and allow their surface moisture to evaporate. Keep this stage to 11–13 minutes over steady low heat and stop when a grain pressed between two fingers has no chalky center.

Toast the split black gram in sesame oil. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over moderate heat for 2–3 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.
Add mustard, peanuts, turmeric, and curry leaves. Keep the pan over medium-low heat for 1–2 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.

Fold the hot tempering into the sorghum, take the pan off the flame. Warm the fat over medium-low heat for 1 minute, let the spice sizzle for 30–45 seconds, and pour the tempering over the dish before its final rest.
For Karnataka Lemon Jowar Chitranna, mix in the lemon juice and salt. Keep the pan over low heat for 1–2 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.
Rest Karnataka Lemon Jowar Chitranna for 5 minutes covered off the burner; fluff the grains once, check the final consistency, and serve warm without prolonged holding.

items.name: Karnataka Coconut Sesame Rice Bath
steps: Set the brown rice, fresh coconut, and sesame seeds in separate bowls and complete the listed rinsing, cutting, or grinding before heating the pan.

Loosen the tender brown rice with a fork and keep it covered while the flavoring is prepared. Work over medium-low heat for 15–17 minutes; continue once a grain pressed between two fingers has no chalky center.

Brown the cashew pieces in ghee, add cumin and curry leaves. Give the spices about 30 seconds before adding the larger pieces, then continue over gentle medium heat for 3–4 minutes, moving the pan often, until the raw aroma is gone.
Stir in the coconut just until fragrant. Keep the pan over low heat for 1–2 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.
Fold the warm mixture and ground sesame through the rice, season. Leave the pan off the flame for 6 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.

items.name: Karnataka Pumpkin Peanut Gojju

ingredients.name: Pumpkin, peeled and cut into cubes

steps: Measure 520 ml (about 2 1/4 cups) water for Karnataka Pumpkin Peanut Gojju; bring it to a full boil, then keep it covered and hot for the additions below.
Sputter mustard and fenugreek in sesame oil. Work over medium-low heat for 7–9 minutes; continue once a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.
Turn the pumpkin cubes through the aromatic fat. Allow 12–14 minutes at gentle medium heat, checking whether a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.
Add the diluted tamarind and simmer until the pumpkin yields while retaining its shape. Aim for an even 2–3 mm thickness; repair cracks before the piece reaches the hot surface.

Stir in the coarse peanuts and grated jaggery, reduce the gojju to a clinging sauce. Maintain steady low heat for 7–9 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a spoon drawn across the base leaves a trail that closes slowly.
Finish with curry leaves. Leave the pan off the flame for 3 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Rest Karnataka Pumpkin Peanut Gojju for 5 minutes covered off the burner; stir once gently, check the final consistency, and serve warm without prolonged holding.

Add the diced ridge gourd and slit chili. Keep the pan over gentle medium heat for 1–2 minutes after the final addition, folding from the bottom so the main pieces remain intact.
Simmer until the vegetable becomes soft and the tovve thickens. Maintain low heat for 10–12 minutes, stirring every 3 minutes, until a thin knife slides through the largest piece without resistance.

Bloom cumin and curry leaves in ghee, stir this tempering through the dal. Warm the fat over medium-low heat for 1 minute, let the spice sizzle for 30–45 seconds, and pour the tempering over the dish before its final rest.
Season just before serving. Leave the pan off the flame for 4 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.

items.name: Karnataka Spinach Mung Bassaru
steps: Prepare 1050 ml (about 4 1/2 cups) hot water before starting Karnataka Spinach Mung Bassaru; keep one small ladle in reserve in case the base tightens early.
For Karnataka Spinach Mung Bassaru, cover the mung beans with at least three times its volume of cool water and soak for 40 minutes; drain for 2 minutes before the first heated step.

Cook the soaked mung until tender, add the spinach. Simmer the pulses over low heat for 15–18 minutes, then add the greens for the final 3–4 minutes, until both components are tender without losing all definition.
Drain off most of the green cooking broth into a second pot. Let it drain for 1 minute without pressing harder than the recipe's texture requires.

Simmer the reserved broth with chopped tomato, cumin, and pepper until it becomes a fragrant, light saaru. Maintain moderate heat for 9–11 minutes, stirring every 4 minutes, until a spoon drawn across the base leaves a trail that closes slowly.
Mash the remaining beans and greens coarsely, season both preparations. Leave the pan off the flame for 5 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
Finish the broth with warm ghee before serving them together. Leave the pan off the flame for 6 minutes, then taste and correct the final balance before serving at the stated temperature.
